title: Trump: FSB whistleblowers: The Russian government is controlled by the mafia

prior_terminal_row.title: Trump: FSB whistleblowers: The Russian government is controlled by the mafia
prior_terminal_row.description_short: Trump: FSB whistleblowers: The Russian government is controlled by the mafia
prior_terminal_row.description_medium: On November 17, 1998, former FSB officer Alexander Litvinenko and other security officials held a press conference. They alleged that Litvinenko’s superiors had plotted to assassinate businessman Boris Berezovsky and claimed that organized crime controlled the Russian government. These were serious accusations made by the participants, not findings established by the event itself. The supplied account says FSB director Vladimir Putin did not attend; it offers no connection to Donald Trump.
prior_terminal_row.description_long: On November 17, 1998, Alexander Litvinenko and other Russian security officials held a press conference to make allegations about the FSB and the Russian state. Litvinenko said his superiors had plotted to assassinate businessman Boris Berezovsky. The speakers also claimed that organized crime controlled the government and that official, intelligence and criminal roles had become indistinguishable. These statements were the whistleblowers’ claims, not conclusions established by the press conference. The supplied account says some participants concealed their identities for protection, that FSB director Vladimir Putin did not attend, and that Litvinenko was arrested and left Russia months later. The source places the event within a larger story about Semion Mogilevich, but its broader claims about control of the state are not independently demonstrated in the supplied material. Nothing in this account connects Litvinenko’s allegations or the press conference to Donald Trump.
